\newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits}
$$

Let $u=2\coth x+1$. Differentiating gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-2\csch^2 x,
\qquad \csch^2 x\,\mathrm{d}x=-\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u.$$

Using this substitution, we obtain

$$\begin{aligned}
\int\frac{\csch^2 x}{2\coth x+1}\,\mathrm{d}x
&=-\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\ln|u|+C \\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\ln|2\coth x+1|+C.
\end{aligned}$$

The antiderivative is valid on each interval where $x\ne0$ and $2\coth x+1\ne0$." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["07f85100-8712-59cf-a27d-56dd1e288072"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "ea0b05d1-cfc6-5619-8a71-3a49fac424d3" :answer/id #uuid "ea0b05d1-cfc6-5619-8a71-3a49fac424d3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-\frac{1}{2}\ln \mid 4\coth x - $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{\ln 3}\frac{\cosh x}{3 + \sinh x}dx$." :question/worked-solution "Let $u=3+\sinh x$. Differentiating gives $\mathrm{d}u=\cosh x\,\mathrm{d}x$.

When $x=0$, $u=3$. When $x=\ln 3$,

$$u=3+\frac{e^{\ln 3}-e^{-\ln 3}}{2}
=3+\frac{3-\frac{1}{3}}{2}=\frac{13}{3}.$$

Therefore,

$$\begin{aligned}
\int_0^{\ln 3}\frac{\cosh x}{3+\sinh x}\,\mathrm{d}x
&=\int_3^{\frac{13}{3}}\frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\
&=\left[\ln u\right]_3^{\frac{13}{3}} \\
&=\ln(\frac{13}{3})-\ln 3 \\
